places.rationale: A raised coral island whose income rests on Australian-funded offshore processing, fishing licences and aid, with very poor health and desalination-dependent water. Close Australian ties make modest gains likely, but its past boom-and-bust and near-total import dependence keep decline and collapse real.

reading.reason: Prices matter most: Nauru imports almost all food, fuel and medicine, so cheaper goods and desalination help, while it owns no AI and sells little labour.

places.rationale: Low atolls face 44-76 cm of sea-level rise, storm surges and salinising groundwater, partly offset by land-reclamation plans and the Falepili Union's migration and security guarantees with Australia. Aid, fishing rents and remittances make modest gains likely, but habitability risk keeps collapse high.

reading.reason: Prices help most as Tuvalu imports nearly everything, but seafarer and seasonal-work remittances face automation, and it owns no AI to share in profits.
